[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is sulfisoxazole (3,4-dimethyl-5-isoxazolyl sulfanilamide); the closest supplied analog is sulfamethoxazole, for which L3 oral-exposure records show substantial systemic exposure after oral dosing (AUC 39.07 µg·h/mL at 60 mg/kg p.o., C111; AUC 25.9 µg·h/mL at 30 mg/kg p.o., C118; Cmax 60.9 mg/L, C104).

L4 records for the sulfanilamide/isoxazole class consistently show high fraction absorbed: sulfamethoxazole absorption increased in disease (C135), sulfamethizole 85% Fa (C175) with Caco-2 permeability (C177), sulfapyridine almost complete absorption (C131, C156, C166), sulfamethazine practically complete absorption (C154, C172) and 99.2% relative absorption as an oral solution (C141), and sulfadimethoxine well absorbed (C153).
L5 Caco-2 data for sulfamethoxazole show moderate A-B permeability (4.5 ± 0.29 ×10^-6 cm/s) with no meaningful efflux (ER 1.3) and high mass balance (C224; duplicated as C188/C182).

L6 records show sulfamethoxazole undergoes CYP2C9-mediated N4-hydroxylation (C244, C275) with genotype-dependent in vitro Clint values (e.g., wild-type recombinant 27.8 ± 10.1 µl/nmol, C229; human liver microsomes 0.68 ± 0.37 µl/nmol/min, C248), but these are pathway-specific intrinsic-clearance measurements, not total hepatic extraction or in vivo F, and do not affirm F < 20%.

L6 high HLM Clint values for non-query isoxazole sulfonamides (17-203 µL/min/mg; C270, C238, C258, C236) are structurally distinct benzylic sulfonamides and are not transferable as low-F evidence for the anilino sulfonamide query.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for sulfisoxazole or sulfamethoxazole is supplied in the records.
No total hepatic clearance, hepatic extraction ratio, or in vivo first-pass data are supplied for the query or closest analog; L6 CYP2C9 N-hydroxylation Clint values are pathway-specific.
Transfer is analogical; no context exactly matches the 3,4-dimethyl-5-isoxazolyl sulfanilamide scaffold.
Formulation effects are unknown; enteric-coated PAS had 0% relative bioavailability (C64, C70), so formulation could modify exposure.
Species and condition differences add uncertainty in extrapolation.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high because L3-L5 evidence for the closest sulfanilamide-isoxazole analog (sulfamethoxazole) and related sulfonamides shows high oral absorption and substantial systemic exposure, with no meaningful efflux; L6 CYP2C9 metabolism records are pathway-specific and do not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%. The physicochemical prior (low neutral fraction, high TPSA) is not sufficient to overturn this.

messages.content:
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L1 contains current-gold constituent measurements. L2 appends other raw gold-source-domain records from those same contexts; all L1 cards remain visible. L3/L4/L5/L6 append one ranked Stage 3 record bundle each; all earlier cards remain visible.","record_sampling":"Each context and level shows a deterministic sample of at most ten raw records. available_record_counts reports the full pool before sampling.
